reason: The cited evidence confirms the lamellar L1₂/B2 structure and the ductile/brittle nature of the phases, but none of the passages mention aging-induced interfacial L1₂ precipitation, its effect on interfacial cohesion, or its role in suppressing microcrack initiation. The key mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the provided references.
premises: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA has a lamellar L1₂ + B2 microstructure
The L1₂ phase is ductile and the B2 phase is brittle
Microcracking initiates at internal lamellar boundaries during room-temperature deformation
Aging at ~650–700 °C can induce coherent nanoscale L1₂ precipitates along lamellar interfaces
Such interfacial precipitates enhance interfacial cohesion and suppress microcrack initiation
